questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Result, ?, and error design”?
options: `?` returns an error to the caller and passes the success value onward.
Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
questions.answer: `?` returns an error to the caller and passes the success value onward.
questions.explanation:
`?` returns an error to the caller and passes the success value onward.
Why: Result<T, E> represents success or failure in the type system; `?` propagates compatible errors through a call chain. Translate concrete errors into useful messages at application boundaries while preserving causes and context in internal layers. Reserve `unwrap()` for small examples or proven invariants where a panic is acceptable.

`Option<T>` represents an expected absence (`None`); `Result<T, E>` represents success or a reportable failure. `?` propagates errors instead of introducing an unnecessary panic, and `main -> Result` can report a top-level failure. Reserve `unwrap()` for tests or proven invariants.
